Prepared for: Executive Leadership Team & Board of DirectorsIssued: November 2026

1Executive Summary

Northwind Analytics delivered a strong third quarter, with growth, retention and profitability all improving over Q2. Quarterly revenue rose 9.3% to $22.3M, and annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached $91.6M, up 8.8% from the prior quarter. Growth was broad-based. The launch of Northwind Insights AI lifted enterprise deal sizes, and our customer success investments cut churn to its lowest level in six quarters.

Bottom line: Q3 shows that the business can grow at a rate near 9% per quarter while expanding margins. The main watch items for Q4 are rising mid-market pricing pressure, weak LATAM results, and sales capacity in the enterprise segment.

North America remains the core of the business, with growth driven by enterprise expansions. EMEA benefited from new data-residency capabilities in Frankfurt. APAC was the fastest-growing region, led by Australia and Singapore. LATAM declined after two delayed renewals and a partner transition, and it is the focus of a Q4 recovery plan.

4Key Wins

1

Northwind Insights AI launched to general availability

The AI-assisted analytics module reached 240 customers within six weeks of launch. Customers who adopted it showed an average 18% uplift in contract value.

2

Three enterprise logos won, each above $1M ARR

New contracts in financial services, healthcare and retail added a combined $3.6M in ARR and validated our move up-market.

3

Churn at a six-quarter low

Proactive health scoring and a dedicated onboarding team cut logo churn to 1.9% and lifted NRR to 111%.

4

EU data residency and SOC 2 Type II renewal

The Frankfurt region went live and our SOC 2 Type II audit passed without exceptions, removing a key blocker in regulated EMEA deals.

5

Efficiency gains across go-to-market

CAC payback improved to 15 months, and operating margin expanded by 2.2 points through improved sales productivity and cloud cost optimization.
